source_review.notes: Checked the official SIAM record for Manber-Myers, Springer/DOI publication metadata for Kasai et al. and Kärkkäinen-Sanders, IEEE DOI metadata for Nong-Zhang-Chan, and the official Cambridge record for Gusfield. Construction claims are limited to their named algorithm and computation model.

evidence: Checked suffix slices, suffix ranks, inverse permutation, predecessor-indexed LCP convention, half-open pattern intervals, LCE/RMQ ranges, offset bounds, and balanced GitHub math delimiters.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The no-empty-suffix convention and zero-based half-open slices remain consistent throughout.

evidence: Recomputed banana and abab suffix orders, adjacent LCP values, pattern intervals, LCE values, longest repeats, and distinct-substring counts.
Exhaustively checked 511 binary texts through length 8, 15,330 pattern queries, 26,106 LCE queries, every adjacent LCP, and every distinct-substring count against direct oracles.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Recomputed the 12-billion-offset width requirement and 10^9-entry array byte/GiB estimates.

evidence: Re-derived pattern-interval contiguity from lexicographic order.
Re-derived Kasai's h-1 reuse rule and amortized linear increment bound.
Re-derived LCE as the minimum adjacent LCP over the suffix-rank interval and distinct-substring count by subtracting previously introduced prefixes.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Prefix-doubling bounds distinguish comparison sorting from radix/counting sorting of integer rank pairs.

evidence: Checked empty text, one symbol, equal symbols, periodic strings, exact and absent patterns, empty-pattern policy, first and last ranks, tied repeats, and long common prefixes.

Checked sentinel collision, cross-document matches, normalization changes, offset overflow, corrupt persisted arrays, mixed generations, result floods, cancellation, and repeated-prefix resource pressure.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Construction and query resource bounds are separated from correctness claims.

evidence: Checked bounded permutation, adjacent order, inverse ranks, LCP length bounds and equality, binary-search partitions, exact result verification, and snapshot identity.
Exhaustive tests checked every permutation, adjacent LCP, LCE RMQ interval, and finite query result in their domain.
invariant_checking.notes: Persisted encoding, separator, width, and generation metadata are part of index validity.

evidence: Reviewed the suffix-array validity theorem from permutation coverage and transitive adjacent order.
Reviewed the pattern-interval theorem's smaller, larger, and early-ending cases.
Reviewed the Kasai reuse lemma and LCE-RMQ theorem, including the precise open/closed endpoints in LCP rank space.
proof_review.notes: The executable suffix-slicing constructor is explicitly an oracle and receives no scalable bound.

evidence: Audited theorem, lemma, proof, invariant, linear, quadratic, worst-case, comparison-sort, word-RAM, exact, sample, and certificate language.
Separated construction-family theorems from Python execution and production sampling evidence.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No unspecified implementation is described as linear-time or constant-time LCE.

evidence: The CPython 3.14.4 snippet exited zero with the exact banana suffix array, LCP, ana occurrences, LCE, and distinct-substring count on macOS 13.7.8 x86_64.
Independent exhaustive finite-domain checks covered 511 texts, 15,330 pattern queries, and 26,106 LCE queries.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Observed behavior is scoped to the recorded environment and finite domains; it is not a performance benchmark.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed immutable representation, suffix-array order, rank inversion, construction families, Kasai LCP, pattern intervals, repeated and distinct substrings, LCE/RMQ, collections, persistence, and validation. Scope leaves suffix-tree and automaton topology to ALGE-056.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed suffix materialization, alphabet and collation stability, sentinel/separator policy, document boundaries, offset width, byte order, peak build storage, external-memory I/O, checksums, generation publication, rollback, pagination, query ordering, cancellation, and adversarial prefixes.

pedagogical_review.notes: The Level-II chapter derives ordering and LCP mechanisms, distinguishes reference code from scalable construction, includes ten distinct construction, query, proof, failure, capacity, and production examples, and ends with five progressive exercises and complete answers.

limitations: Internal source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical review only; no external academic, performance, storage-engine, internationalization, security, or operational review is claimed. Results remain conditional on the stated suffix convention, symbol order, construction model, immutable snapshot, collection boundary, offset, and resource assumptions.
